title: The positive-power section-generation locus is stable under a square-condition action
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $H\to S$ a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with an $S$-group scheme structure and connected fibres $H_s=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-connected-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme means a scheme $H$ with $S$-morphisms $m:H\times_SH\to H$, $i:H\to H$, $e:S\to H$ satisfying associativity, identity and inverse identities; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $X\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation, equipped with an action $a:H\times_SX\to X$, meaning that $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(g,a(h,x))=a(gh,x)$ as morphism identities. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For any $S$-scheme $B$, put $X_B=X\times_SB$, with structure map $q_B:X_B\to B$, and let $M_B$ be the tensor pullback of $M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $g\in H(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,H)$ let $\tau_g:X_B\to X_B$ be the action $x\mapsto gx$. Say that $M$ satisfies the square condition for this action if, for every such $B$ and every $g,h\in H(B)$, there is an invertible $\mathcal O_B$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\cong\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N.$$ All tensors are module sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This is equality of the translation differences in the group of invertible-module classes modulo modules pulled back from $B$; no coherence or chosen isomorphisms are part of the condition. Assume that $M$ satisfies this square condition. Put $$E=\bigcup_{n\geq1}\ \bigcup_{s\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})} X_s,$$ where $X_s$ is the nonvanishing open of the section $s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]; no affineness requirement is imposed on these opens. Then the image on underlying points of $a:H\times_SE\to X$ equals $E$. In particular, the action carries $H\times_SE$ into the open subscheme $E$.

source.place: Guo, section 5.6 (square condition as Picard-admissibility), Lemma 6.3(ii), printed p.15 (smooth separated finite-presentation specialization); March 31, 2026 version, read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $E_n=\bigcup_{s\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})}X_s$ for $n>0$. Finite presentation includes quasi-compactness, so $X$ is quasi-compact since the base is affine; $X\to S$ is separated by hypothesis. Each $M^{\otimes n}$ is invertible and hence quasi-coherent. The generating-locus definition identifies each $X_s$ with an open subscheme. Thus $E_n$ and $E=\bigcup_{n>0}E_n$ are open. These observations verify the compactness, separatedness and quasi-coherence hypotheses needed for flat cohomology base change below.

source.place: Guo, Lemma 6.3(i)–(ii), printed p.15, with the local-ring flat-base-change argument expanded; online March 31, 2026 version, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix $z\in|H\times_SE_n|$ and let $K=\kappa(z)$. Its components give $h\in H(K)$ and $y\in E_n(K)$; set $x=h y\in X(K)$ and let $s\in S$ be their base point. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega/K$. The fibre $H_s$ is connected and has its rational identity point, so it remains connected over $\Omega$. The group scheme $H_\Omega$ is locally of finite type: on affine presentation charts, tensoring a finite presentation $R[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ with $\Omega$ gives the same finite generators and relations over $\Omega$. Here finite-presentation base change supplies that assertion, and finite presentation implies finite type by forgetting the relations. Apply the identity-component theorem over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$: the identity component is geometrically irreducible and, because $H_\Omega$ is connected, it is all of $H_\Omega$. In particular $|H_\Omega|$ is irreducible.

source.place: Guo, Lemma 6.3(i)–(ii), printed p.15, with the local-ring flat-base-change argument expanded; online March 31, 2026 version, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $\alpha:H_\Omega\to X_\Omega$ be $v\mapsto v x_\Omega$, and let $W=\alpha^{-1}((E_n)_\Omega)$. This is open and contains $h_\Omega^{-1}$, since $h_\Omega^{-1}x_\Omega=y_\Omega$. Inversion is an automorphism of $H_\Omega$, so $W\cap i^{-1}(W)$ is the intersection of two nonempty opens. It is nonempty by irreducibility. Choose a point $u$ of this intersection, put $L=\kappa(u)$ and denote its corresponding element of $H(L)$ by $g$. Then both $g x_L$ and $g^{-1}x_L$ belong to the inverse image of $E_n$ in $X_L$. By the definition of this inverse image as a union of inverse images of the $X_s$, there are original global sections $s_+,s_-\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})$ whose values at these two points, respectively, are nonzero. No assertion that sections commute with the nonflat base change to $L$ is used.

source.place: Guo, Lemma 6.3(i)–(ii), printed p.15, with the local-ring flat-base-change argument expanded; online March 31, 2026 version, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $p\in H$ be the image of $g:\operatorname{Spec}L\to H$, let $R=\mathcal O_{H,p}$, and put $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The canonical map $B\to H$ is flat; $H\to S$ is flat because it is smooth. Their composite $B\to S$ is flat, and the affine flatness criterion gives that $R$ is a flat $A$-algebra. The canonical map $c:B\to H$ is an element $g_B\in H(B)$. By the local-spectrum bijection, $g:\operatorname{Spec}L\to H$ corresponds to the pair $(p,\varphi)$ with $\varphi:R\to L$ its local stalk map. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}L\to B$ sends the point to the closed point, and $c$ maps that point to $p$ with stalk map the identity of $R$. Hence $c\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ has the same pair $(p,\varphi)$, so it equals $g$. Pairing this map with $x_L$ gives an $L$-valued point $\widetilde x$ of $X_B$. At this point $g_B$ specializes to $g$. Notice that flatness is asserted for $B\to S$, not for $\operatorname{Spec}L\to S$.

source.place: Guo, Lemma 6.3(i)–(ii), printed p.15, with the local-ring flat-base-change argument expanded; online March 31, 2026 version, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the square condition on $B$ to $g_B,g_B^{-1}$. Since their product is the identity, it gives $M_B^{\otimes2}\cong\tau_{g_B}^*M_B\otimes\tau_{g_B^{-1}}^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N$ for an invertible $N$ on $B$. An invertible module on $\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $R$ local, is trivial: its trivializing open around the closed point is the entire spectrum, since every principal open containing that point is the entire spectrum. Choose such a trivialization, and take the $n$th tensor power of the displayed isomorphism. Pullback is functorial and commutes with tensor powers. Pull back $s_+$ along $\tau_{g_B}$ after base change, and $s_-$ along $\tau_{g_B^{-1}}$; their tensor product therefore gives a section $r\in\Gamma(X_B,(M_B)^{\otimes2n})$. The pullback nonvanishing statement shows both factors are nonzero at $\widetilde x$. In a one-dimensional vector space over $L$, their tensor product is nonzero. Consequently $r(\widetilde x)\ne0$.

source.place: Guo, Lemma 6.3(i)–(ii), printed p.15, with the local-ring flat-base-change argument expanded; online March 31, 2026 version, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Identify $(M_B)^{\otimes2n}$ with the pullback of $M^{\otimes2n}$. In degree zero, cohomology is global sections. Apply the separated flat-base-change theorem with the compact scheme $X$, its separated structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the quasi-coherent module $M^{\otimes2n}$ and the flat $A$-algebra $R$. Its specific comparison is surjective, and sends $b\otimes t$ to $b\,t_B$. Hence the section from step 5 has the form $r=\sum_{j=1}^k b_j(t_j)_B$, with $t_j\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes2n})$ and $b_j\in R$. If all $t_j$ vanished at the underlying image $x_0\in X$ of $x_L$, their pullbacks would vanish at $\widetilde x$, so the displayed sum would vanish there. This contradicts step 5. Thus some $t_j$ is nonzero at $x_0$, giving $x_0\in E_{2n}\subseteq E$. This argument uses the canonical comparison formula, not merely an abstract isomorphism of the two modules.

source.place: Guo, Lemma 6.3(i)–(ii), printed p.15, with the local-ring flat-base-change argument expanded; online March 31, 2026 version, local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Every point of $H\times_SE$ belongs to $H\times_SE_n$ for some $n>0$, since its second component lies in one of the $E_n$. Steps 2–6 therefore show $a(|H\times_SE|)\subseteq|E|$. Conversely the identity section gives $E\to H\times_SE$, and its composite with the action is the inclusion of $E$ into $X$. This gives the reverse inclusion on underlying points, hence equality. Since $E$ is open and the inverse image of $E$ under the restricted action is the whole source, restricting its continuous map and its structure-sheaf morphism to $E$ yields the asserted morphism $H\times_SE\to E$.

source.place: Guo, Lemma 6.3(i)–(ii), printed p.15, with the local-ring flat-base-change argument expanded; online March 31, 2026 version, local copy WANTED.

lean.statement: theorem square_action_generation_locus_stable (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] (H : Over S) [GrpObj H] [Smooth H.hom] [IsSeparated H.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation H.hom] [QuasiCompact H.hom] [QuasiSeparated H.hom] (hH : ∀ s : S, ConnectedSpace (H.hom.fiber s)) (X : Over S) [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [QuasiSeparated X.hom] [ModObj H X] (M : X.left.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (hsquare : ∀ (B : Over S) (g h : B ⟶ H), ∃ N : B.left.Modules, N.IsInvertible ∧ Nonempty (((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (((snd X B ≫ (g * h)) • fst X B).left)).obj M ⊗ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (fst X B).left).obj M) ≅ (((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (((snd X B ≫ g) • fst X B).left)).obj M ⊗ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (((snd X B ≫ h) • fst X B).left)).obj M) ⊗ (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (snd X B).left).obj N))) : ∃ E : X.left.Opens, (E : Set X.left) = ⋃ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n) (s : (M.tensorPow n).val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)), Scheme.Modules.nonvanishingLocus (M.tensorPow n) s ∧ Set.image (γ[H, X].left.base) ((snd H X).left.base ⁻¹' (E : Set X.left)) = (E : Set X.left) ∧ ∃ aE : (H ⊗ Over.mk (E.ι ≫ X.hom)).left ⟶ E.toScheme, aE ≫ E.ι = ((H ◁ Over.homMk E.ι) ≫ γ[H, X]).left
lean.note: The square condition is written directly as an existential isomorphism hypothesis on every B-point pair. Translation pullback of M_B is expressed by tensor pullback along the composite (x,b) ↦ g(b)x, canonically identified by pullback composition. The conclusion names the specified union as an open E, states equality of its action image on all underlying points, and gives the restricted action factorization.
